questions.stem: Which of the following is the correct state of water?
questions.solution: The correct state of water is solid, as water freezes into ice at temperatures below 0°C. Liquid is incorrect because it refers to water in its fluid state, not the specific state being asked. Gas is incorrect because it refers to water vapor, which is not the state in question. Plasma is incorrect because it is a high-energy state of matter not typically associated with water under normal conditions.

hi.stem: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सी जल की सही अवस्था है?
hi.solution: जल की सही अवस्था ठोस है क्योंकि जल 0°C से नीचे के तापमान पर बर्फ में जम जाता है। तरल गलत है क्योंकि यह जल की तरल अवस्था को संदर्भित करता है, न कि पूछे गए विशिष्ट अवस्था को। गैस गलत है क्योंकि यह जल के वाष्प को संदर्भित करता है, जो प्रश्न में अवस्था नहीं है। प्लाज्मा गलत है क्योंकि यह ऊंची ऊर्जा वाली पदार्थ की अवस्था है जो सामान्य परिस्थितियों में जल के साथ जुड़ी नहीं होती है।

questions.stem: What happens when light rays fall on an opaque substance?
questions.solution: Light does not pass through an opaque substance because the material blocks all light. Some light passing through would describe a translucent or transparent material, not an opaque one. All light passing through is incorrect as it contradicts the definition of opacity. Light bending around the substance is a description of diffraction, not the behavior of light with opaque materials.

questions.stem: Which of the following properties of a substance is determined by how tightly its particles hold each other?
questions.solution: The state of a substance, such as solid, liquid, or gas, is determined by how tightly its particles are held together. This is because the strength of the forces between particles affects their arrangement and movement. Mass, volume, and density are properties that depend on the amount of matter and its distribution, not the strength of particle interactions.

questions.stem: What does it mean if oil floats on water?
choices: Oil is less dense than water
Oil has the same density as water
questions.solution: Oil floats on water because it is less dense than water, which means it has a lower mass per unit volume. This is a fundamental principle of buoyancy and density. The other options are incorrect because oil is not denser than water, nor does it have the same density, and oil is not a solid.

questions.stem: Which of the following describes the gaseous state of a substance?
choices: Particles are very close to each other and hold each other tightly
Particles are slightly further apart and loosely bound
Particles scatter everywhere in the available space
Particles move in a fixed position
questions.solution: The gaseous state is characterized by particles that are not held together and can move freely, which means they scatter everywhere in the available space. In contrast, particles in solids are very close and fixed in position, while those in liquids are slightly further apart but still loosely bound. This matches the behavior of gases, where particles have high kinetic energy and minimal attraction between them.

questions.stem: What happens to the particles of a substance when it is in the solid state?
choices: They move freely in all directions

questions.stem: A student wants to determine if a sample of gold is pure. What information should they compare?
choices: The density of the sample with the density of water

The density of the sample with the known density of pure gold
The mass of the sample with the volume of the sample
questions.solution: The correct option is to compare the density of the sample with the known density of pure gold because the density of a substance is a unique physical property that does not change with the amount of the substance. Comparing with water or other metals does not provide a direct way to assess purity, and comparing mass with volume only gives density, not a comparison to a known standard.
